mission_07: Non-IID (non-Independently and Identically Distributed) data is the most challenging aspect of federated learning. In real-world scenarios, each client's data distribution differs significantly from others - different users type different words, different hospitals see different patient populations. This mission implements three strategies to handle non-IID data. Dirichlet-based partitioning creates realistic non-IID splits by sampling client class proportions from a Dirichlet distribution - lower alpha values create more skewed distributions. Class-balanced loss reweights the training objective to compensate for label imbalance on each client. The shared representation approach splits the model into a global base (shared across all clients) and local heads (client-specific), allowing shared feature extraction while maintaining personalized classification.
